name: Cross-border mule and payment-chain laundering of fraud proceeds
description: Proceeds of authorised-push and online fraud are moved rapidly across several mule accounts, payment institutions, correspondent chains and crypto off-ramps in different jurisdictions, so that recall and freezing requests lag behind the funds. Each hop can look unremarkable alone; the signal lies in speed, chain length, data gaps in payment messages and repeated fraud-related recalls. Complements ML-MULE and FR-APP, which focus on single-account and victim-side views.

sources.text: FATF, INTERPOL and Egmont Group, Illicit Financial Flows from Cyber-enabled Fraud (2023)
FATF, Recommendation 16 (payment transparency) revisions and Interpretive Note (2025)
FATF, Guidance on Correspondent Banking Services (2016)

exposure.rationale: Multi-hop mule chain via PSPs, correspondents and off-ramps.

indicators.name: Rapid pass-through of received funds
indicators.desc: Funds received into an account are forwarded onward within a very short period, often in near-equal amounts and leaving minimal balance.
indicators.ctx: Cross-border fraud proceeds are forwarded onward within minutes or hours in near-equal amounts, leaving minimal balance at each mule hop.
indicators.fp: Legitimate payment intermediaries, treasury sweeps and agents routinely pass funds through quickly.

indicators.name: Rapid movement through correspondent or private banking channels
indicators.canon: Rapid movement through correspondent or private banking channels
indicators.desc: Large sums move quickly through several banks and jurisdictions after arrival, with no hold period.
indicators.ctx: Large sums transit several banks and jurisdictions after arrival, outpacing recall and freeze requests.
indicators.fp: Treasury and liquidity management can cause fast movements.

indicators.name: Missing, incomplete or placeholder originator and beneficiary information
indicators.canon: Missing, incomplete or placeholder originator and beneficiary information
indicators.desc: Payment messages omit, truncate or use generic placeholder data for originator or beneficiary details.
indicators.ctx: Incoming or outgoing payment messages carry placeholder, truncated or missing originator and beneficiary data, hindering alignment checks and tracing along the chain.

indicators.name: Sender or intermediary with history of message-quality deficiencies
indicators.canon: Sender or intermediary with history of message-quality deficiencies
indicators.desc: Peer institution frequently sends payments with data gaps.
indicators.ctx: A particular peer institution or payment provider repeatedly forwards fraud-linked payments with data gaps.

indicators.name: Use of multiple accounts to move funds
indicators.canon: Use of multiple accounts to move funds
indicators.desc: Customer spreads activity across many accounts, products or institutions.
indicators.ctx: Funds are spread across many accounts, wallets and institutions per customer or linked group to fragment the trail and stay under monitoring limits.

indicators.name: Rapid sequential conversions across many asset types
indicators.canon: Rapid sequential conversions across many asset types
indicators.desc: Funds received are swapped through several tokens or stablecoins in quick succession with no apparent trading rationale before withdrawal.
indicators.ctx: At the crypto off-ramp, proceeds are swapped through multiple assets or stablecoins in quick succession before withdrawal to a new platform or wallet.
indicators.fp: Active traders, arbitrageurs and market makers.

indicators.name: Rapid cash-out after cross-chain arrival
indicators.desc: Assets arriving via bridge are sold into fiat or stablecoin and withdrawn within a short window.
indicators.ctx: Assets arriving by cross-chain bridge are sold into fiat or stablecoin and withdrawn quickly, completing the hop from fraud proceeds to cash-out.

indicators.name: Cross-border corridor with known abuse typologies
indicators.canon: Cross-border corridor with known abuse typologies
indicators.desc: Payments use corridors identified in typology reports as high risk, including regions where informal value transfer is prevalent.
indicators.ctx: Chains repeatedly use corridors and intermediary jurisdictions named in fraud typology reports as common cash-out routes.
indicators.fp: Corridors are used mainly by legitimate remittance senders.

indicators.name: Repeated fraud recalls or return requests against the same receiving account or originating institution
indicators.canon: Repeated fraud recalls or return requests against the same receiving account or originating institution
indicators.desc: A receiving account, or flows from a given originating institution, attract multiple recall, return or fraud-notification requests in a short period, often followed by funds already having left.
indicators.ctx: Several recalls arriving from different foreign institutions against one account is a strong indicator of a cross-border mule hop and justifies immediate restriction and reporting.
indicators.fp: Operational errors, duplicate payments, disputed commercial transactions and a single large fraud event hitting one account can generate several recalls without mule activity.

indicators.name: Counterparty institution slow or unresponsive to fraud recall and information requests
indicators.canon: Counterparty institution slow or unresponsive to fraud recall and information requests
indicators.desc: A correspondent, payment institution or exchange repeatedly fails to act on freeze, recall or request-for-information messages in time, or the same beneficiary institution appears in many fraud cases.
indicators.ctx: Weak responsiveness at downstream hops lets proceeds disperse; it informs counterparty risk rating and routing decisions.
indicators.fp: Time-zone differences, legal process requirements in the counterparty's jurisdiction and capacity limits can delay legitimate responses.

added.subject: Add 9 typologies from reference review (market abuse, complicit FI, sham legal, sports, freeports, pensions, transfer pricing, scam compounds, cross-border mules)
